                          leaderLength: 40, joint: "foot_L")

        cues: [
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "back",
                title: "Spine Position",
                intro: "The back stays long from the hips to the head, the neck in line and the eyes on the floor.",
                why: "A neutral spine keeps the bend at the hips, so the hamstrings and glutes lengthen and do the lifting. Letting the back round is one of the most common RDL errors, often once the hips have run out of hinge and the hands keep reaching.",
                mistake: "Rounding the upper back and dropping the head to reach lower.",
                correct: "Brace before each rep, keep the chest open and the chin lightly tucked, and let the trunk tip only as far as the hips can hinge."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "hinge",
                title: "Hinge and Reach",
                intro: "The hips push back as the free leg reaches behind, the trunk and leg tipping together like a seesaw.",
                why: "Pushing the hips back is what stretches the standing leg's hamstrings and glute, and the free leg reaching behind balances the chest so the hips can travel back without tipping you forward. Even with no weight in the hands, a single-leg deadlift worked the standing hip's gluteus maximus and medius moderately in one study.",
                mistake: "Reaching the hands for the floor while the hips stay over the foot and the free leg hangs down.",
                correct: "Push the free heel back toward the wall behind you as the hips go back, and stop when the trunk and free leg are close to level or the hips will not travel further."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "square",
                title: "Level Hips",
                intro: "Both hip bones face the floor and the free leg's toes point straight down.",
                why: "Standing on one leg, the side muscles of the standing hip, the gluteus medius above all, have to hold the pelvis level; a barbell single-leg deadlift drew clearly more gluteus medius than a two-leg deadlift. When the free hip rolls open, the pelvis turns instead of staying square and that control is lost.",
                mistake: "The free hip rolling open toward the ceiling, the free leg swinging out to the side with its toes turned out.",
                correct: "Keep the belt buckle pointing at the floor and the free toes pointing down, and let the leg rise straight behind you, not out to the side."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "knee",
                title: "Standing Knee",
                intro: "The left, standing knee keeps the same soft bend from top to bottom; the right leg is the free leg.",
                why: "A small, fixed bend lets the hips travel back so the hamstrings take the stretch. Bending the knee more as you go down turns the hinge into a one-leg squat and hands work to the thigh muscles, as bent-knee deadlifts do. In a single-leg RDL study the standing knee was held at about 15 degrees of bend throughout.",
                mistake: "The standing knee bending further as the chest lowers, the hips sinking toward the floor.",
                correct: "Unlock the knee a little before you start, hold that angle and push the hips back, not down."
            ),
            TechniqueCue(
                id: "balance",
                title: "Balance",
                intro: "The whole standing foot stays planted, the weight over its middle.",
                why: "One foot is the only base, so the hips moving back has to be matched by the chest and free leg moving the other way to keep the weight over the middle of the foot. Once you rock onto the toes or the heel, the hips stop hinging and the rep turns into a scramble for balance.",
                mistake: "Rocking forward onto the toes, the standing heel lifting, as the chest lowers.",
                correct: "Grip the floor with the heel, big toe and little toe, move slowly, and master this unloaded version before holding weights."
            )

            MuscleActivation(name: "Hamstrings", rank: .primary, fraction: 0.62),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Gluteus Maximus", rank: .primary, fraction: 0.60),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Gluteus Medius", rank: .primary, fraction: 0.60),
            MuscleActivation(name: "Erector Spinae", rank: .secondary, fraction: 0.34)
        ],

        setup: [

            "Rest the right toes lightly on the floor just behind you.",
            "Let both arms hang straight down, palms facing in.",
            "Brace your trunk, hinge for all your reps, then switch to the right leg."

        ),

    )
